newsitem.title: UK: Pregnant IRA suspect wanted in Germany refused bail.
newsitem.headline: Pregnant IRA suspect wanted in Germany refused bail.

text.p: Roisin McAliskey, wanted by German authorites for attempted murder in connection with an IRA mortar attack on a British army base, was refused bail and remanded in custody on Wednesday to await extradition hearings.

The 25-year-old daughter of Bernadette McAliskey, nee Devlin, a former nationalist member of parliament and prominent republican in the 1960s, was arrested last week along with 28-year-old James Corry.
Both are suspected of involvement in the attack on a British army base near the northwest German town of Osnabrueck last summer.

The German authorities, who applied for more time to prepare their case, objected to the bail request by McAliskey, who is more than four months pregnant. She is being held in Britain's Belmarsh high-security prison in southeast London.
"I fail to be surprised at the racism and inhumanity of the British state," her mother, who has been unable to see her, told reporters after the hearing.
The army base attack was one of the IRA's least successful in its 25-year fight against British rule in Northern Ireland. Only one of three mortar bombs exploded. No one was injured.
But it was the first IRA attack in continental Europe following the end of its 17-month ceasefire in February.
The guerrilla group has set off a series of bombs in Britain and staged a car bombing at the British army's headquarters in Northern Ireland which killed one soldier.
Last month British bomb experts defused a huge bomb left outside a police headquarters in Londonderry.
